transcript:
---

[SIMULATION TRANSCRIPT — automated evaluation]

Hiring Manager: Tell me about yourself — specifically what makes you a strong fit for this role.

Candidate: I'm a Senior Software Engineer with five years of experience building distributed systems. Most recently, I personally designed and shipped a distributed caching layer that cut our API latency by 25% and improved application performance by 30%. Before that, I led a team of three engineers to deliver a cloud-based analytics platform that drove a 50% increase in user engagement. I'm targeting Staff because I want to move from individual ownership to platform-level impact across multiple teams.

Hiring Manager: When you say you "led a team of three" — what specifically was your role versus the team's?

Candidate: I owned the architecture decisions. I chose a microservices design over a monolith and wrote the ADR documenting the tradeoffs, because I knew the team would be maintaining this long-term without me. I established the initial patterns via the first few PRs, ran weekly syncs to track cross-team dependencies with product and data, and unblocked engineers when they hit ambiguity. The engineers owned individual service implementations — I owned the shape of the system and the decisions that affected everyone.

Hiring Manager: What almost went wrong?

Candidate: I underestimated the complexity of data consistency across services. I made the call to use eventual consistency to keep services decoupled, but about six weeks in we hit a user-facing bug where stale data surfaced in the dashboard. I had to own that my tradeoff had a real cost. We added a change-data-capture layer to handle the critical read paths and I updated the ADR to document what we learned, so the next team in that space wouldn't repeat the same mistake.
